## Paper

Conditional Cooperation and Voluntary Contributions to Public Goods

## World

public_goods

## Institution

Reputation and information variants.

## Agent type

Conditional cooperators or learning agents reacting to observed social information.

## Theoretical benchmark

Contribution can depend on beliefs/observations about others' contributions.

## Learning setup

Repeated public-goods interaction with reputation or restricted/shared information.

## Metrics

Contribution response, sustainability, welfare, reputation bonuses, information-condition deltas.

## Main result

Subjects in the partners condition contributed significantly more to the public good than those in the strangers condition; contributions in the partners condition fluctuated on a high level before decreasing, while strangers' contributions showed continual decay.

## What they prove

The paper provides experimental evidence for conditional-cooperation patterns: contributions differ between partners and strangers conditions and respond to repeated-group information. Treat this as behavioral evidence, not a formal guarantee for artificial agents.

## What they only simulate

Experimental contribution behavior over repeated public-goods interactions.

## What they do NOT test

Long-term sustainability of contributions; impact of varying group sizes or returns on contributions

## What we need to reproduce

Information/reputation variants should be judged by contribution response and sustainability, not only reward bonuses.

## How our project differs

The paper studies human conditional cooperation. This repo tests whether stylized information/reputation hooks create analogous state changes in learners.

## Implementation obligations

Observable contribution/reputation signal; information restriction transform; contribution and sustainability deltas; accounting-vs-state classification.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

Public Goods reputation and information_restriction outputs; institution-effect validation.

## Failure modes to audit

Reputation increases reward without changing contribution; information restriction changes observation label only; no measured state delta.

## Project code comparison

Compare Conditional Cooperation and Voluntary Contributions to Public Goods to Public Goods reputation and information-restriction rows. The repo should separate reward shaping from actual cooperative behavior.
